description: Device ingest leg for ApkSession: pull real 4K/HEVC clips off an Android device and transfer them resumably, surviving app kill, process kill, network drop and server restart, reusing the existing session-folder contract, dashboard and token gate. Deliverable includes a measured INGEST_NOTES.md, not just working code.

qualityGates.python: ./tool/tests/run.sh must print PASS (last line), using the pinned .venv via ./adrd or .venv/bin/python
qualityGates.kotlin: ./gradlew lint test assembleDebug must pass from ingest/android
qualityGates.ui: Seen running on the demo35 AVD with a screenshot saved under the session's ingest/ folder - a green build is not proof

userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Kotlin + Compose module that compiles and runs on the emulator, so that later stories add behaviour instead of bootstrapping a project inside one iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: Create ingest/android/ as a Gradle project: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose + Material 3, minSdk 26, targetSdk 35
Single empty Compose activity that renders the app name and a placeholder text line
./gradlew assembleDebug produces an APK
APK installs and launches on the demo35 AVD; capture a screenshot to ingest/android/proof/US-001.png
Add ingest/android/.gitignore covering build/, .gradle/, local.properties, *.apk so no artifact is committed
Do not modify any file under tool/scripts/adrd/ - this story is additive only
./gradlew lint test passes
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-10-31 on branch ralph/apksession-device-ingest. ingest/android/ scaffolded: Kotlin 2.0.21, AGP 8.7.3, Gradle 8.14 (cached), Compose BOM 2024.12.01, Material 3, minSdk 26, targetSdk 35, namespace dev.mrvishwet.adrd.ingest. userStories.title: Add chunked upload endpoints to the existing dashboard server
userStories.description: As the pipeline, I need an endpoint that accepts numbered chunks and assembles them, so that a transfer can stop and start without losing work.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /ingest/<session>/init accepts {filename, size, sha256, chunk_size} and returns upload_id; calling init again for the same file returns the existing upload_id (idempotent)
PUT /ingest/<session>/<upload_id>/chunk/<n> stores one chunk; re-sending an already-stored chunk returns 200, not 4xx
GET /ingest/<session>/<upload_id>/status returns the set of stored chunk indices
POST /ingest/<session>/<upload_id>/complete assembles in index order and returns 409 naming the missing ranges when any index is absent
complete verifies SHA-256 of the assembled file against the init value and fails loudly on mismatch
Reject any filename containing a path separator or '..' - assert 403 in a test, matching the existing path-traversal test style in tool/tests/run.sh
All chunk and assembled files are written only inside the session folder, under ingest/
Every new route requires the existing access token; the index page must not leak session names without it, as already enforced elsewhere
Add the new endpoint tests to tool/tests/run.sh so they run with no device attached
./tool/tests/run.sh prints PASS
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-10-31 on the host, no device involved. Routes added to the existing dashboard server in tool/scripts/adrd/watch.py (do_POST/do_PUT + GET status branch); all disk logic in new tool/scripts/adrd/ingest.py. upload_id is deterministic (sha256(filename+sha256) first 16 hex) so init is idempotent by construction; chunks stored at ingest/uploads/<id>/chunks/<n> via temp+fsync+rename; oversize body refused with 413 before being read (body length > chunk_size), wrong-length body refused with 400; complete assembles in index order streaming sha256, returns 409 naming missing ranges, and 409s loudly on sha mismatch keeping chunks for diagnosis; filename with a separator or .. gets 403; every route passes the existing token gate. Tests: tool/tests/test_ingest.py (15 pytest cases, all passing in 7.8s via .venv/bin/python -m pytest) and an ingest round trip + pytest invocation added to tool/tests/run.sh, which printed PASS end to end. pytest 9.2.0 was pip-installed into .venv to run the suite.

userStories.title: Chunk reader with bounded memory and an atomic checkpoint
userStories.description: As the uploader, I need to read a bounded slice of a large file and remember where I got to, so that resume is a lookup rather than a re-scan.
acceptanceCriteria: Reads chunk n via random access (seek + fixed-size read), not by scanning from the start
Peak heap stays under 16 MB while reading a 2 GB sparse file at 4 MB chunk size; assert with a test that measures, not one that assumes
Checkpoint record holds upload_id, chunk_size, next_index, source_size, source_sha256, source_generation_id
Checkpoint is written only AFTER the server acks that chunk; a test asserts a crash between read and ack replays that chunk rather than skipping it
Checkpoint write is atomic (temp file + rename)
Unit tests run on the host JVM with no device attached
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Pick real device videos and read their metadata
userStories.description: As a user, I want to pick clips from the device so I am testing against actual camera files rather than fixtures I generated myself.
acceptanceCriteria: Photo picker used on Android 13+; READ_MEDIA_VIDEO requested, no all-files permission
Resolved from a content:// URI, not only a real path - a test exercises a content URI
Displays codec, width x height, bitrate and byte size from MediaMetadataRetriever before any transfer starts
A 4K HEVC clip is visibly identifiable in the list (codec + resolution shown together)
Selecting a file produces a source_generation_id that changes if the underlying file changes
Verify on the demo35 AVD with a screenshot to ingest/android/proof/US-004.png showing a real clip's metadata
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Happy-path transfer wired end to end over loopback
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the picker, reader, checkpoint and server endpoints connected so that one clip moves successfully before I harden any failure mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Selecting a clip and pressing Upload transfers it to the running dashboard server on 127.0.0.1:8734
Transfer uses the US-003 checkpoint and the US-002 endpoints; no parallel reimplementation of either
Assembled file on the server is byte-identical to the source (SHA-256 match reported by the client)
A scripted end-to-end run completes for a 200 MB file and for a 0-byte file
Nothing outside the session folder is written
./tool/tests/run.sh prints PASS
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Run the transfer through WorkManager so it survives leaving the app
userStories.description: As a user, I want the upload to keep going when I leave the app, because a multi-gigabyte clip is never foreground time.
acceptanceCriteria: Transfer driven by WorkManager with a networkType constraint; one worker per chunk-batch so retry granularity is a batch, not the whole job
am force-stop mid-upload then relaunch: resumes from the last acked chunk and completes; proven by a scripted test, not a manual observation
Device reboot mid-upload: transfer resumes; if WorkManager does not restore the enqueue, the app re-enqueues from the persisted checkpoint on start and a test proves that path
Foreground service used only if genuinely required; if used, correct foregroundServiceType and Android 14 permission handling, and state in the commit message whether it was needed
No polling loop faster than 1 s; worker finishes and leaves no resident notification
Verify the resume-after-force-stop on demo35 and save proof to ingest/android/proof/US-006.png
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Backoff and recovery on a link that drops
userStories.description: As a user on bad network, I want the transfer to back off and recover rather than restart or silently stall.
acceptanceCriteria: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped, and a bounded attempt budget that surfaces a terminal failed state instead of retrying forever
Airplane mode toggled mid-upload on the AVD: pauses, then on restore resumes from the last acked chunk with zero duplicate assembled bytes
Server killed and restarted mid-upload: client recovers via the status endpoint rather than assuming
HTTP 5xx and connection-reset paths each covered by a test against a local fault-injecting stub
A response meaning 'already have this chunk' is treated as success, not error
Terminal failure leaves the checkpoint intact so a later attempt continues
Do not introduce a reconnect loop without backoff - NOTES.md already flags that as an existing defect elsewhere in the portfolio
./tool/tests/run.sh prints PASS
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Progress UI derived from server acknowledgements
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want to see what has actually been acknowledged so far, so that the progress bar means something.
acceptanceCriteria: Progress computed from server-acked chunk count, never from bytes handed to the socket
Shows MB transferred, MB total, current throughput and a rolling ETA
Throughput is a moving average over the last N acks; a test feeds a synthetic ack sequence and asserts the displayed value
After a resume, progress starts at the correct value rather than jumping to 0%
0-byte and single-chunk files produce no division-by-zero and no NaN ETA
Verify on the demo35 AVD with a real clip and save a screenshot of a mid-transfer state to ingest/android/proof/US-008.png
./gradlew lint test passes

userStories.title: Integrity verification and playback through the dashboard
userStories.description: As the pipeline, I need to know the file on the server is the file that was on the phone, and that it still plays.
acceptanceCriteria: Client computes the source SHA-256 as a streaming digest without loading the file whole
Report the measured cost of that digest, including whether it forces a second full read of the file
A corrupted-chunk test (flip one byte before sending) is detected at complete and is not silently assembled; chunks are kept for diagnosis
Assembled file is registered so the existing dashboard can serve it and it plays back
Ingest artifacts are served on their own path and are NOT routed through the masked/unmasked de-branding video path
Existing proof and sweep stages behave unchanged

userStories.title: Write INGEST_NOTES.md with measured findings
userStories.description: As the author, I want the numbers this leg produced written down, including the ones that surprised me, because that is the part that is hard to fake.
acceptanceCriteria: INGEST_NOTES.md at the ApkSession root, same voice and evidence discipline as NOTES.md
Reports measured throughput by chunk size for at least 1, 4 and 8 MB over the tunnel
Reports resume cost as a function of file size, and real time to move a 1 GB clip over the quick tunnel versus plain loopback
Documents how the quick tunnel behaves under a long sustained PUT, including whether it drops, and what the client did about it
Contains at least one finding that contradicts an assumption held before the run, stated as such; if nothing was contradicted, say so and say what was expected
If adaptive chunk sizing is implemented, the rule driving it is written down with its measured benefit; if not implemented, state that rather than implying it
Explicitly lists what was NOT tested (iOS, real cellular network, HEVC-specific handling)
Every number in the document is reproducible from a command recorded in the document
